SHELF SAMPLES / 01
System Design
Start with the job
Before drawing components, establish who uses the
system, what they need to do, and what failure would
mean. An architecture solves a particular set of
constraints.
Need Constraint Decision
For a personal PDF reader, local access, data integrity
and fast navigation may matter more than
multi-region availability. Do not pay for complexity
that the task does not require.
A useful question: what must still work when the
internet does not?
SHELF / ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 1

pages.canonicalText:
SHELF SAMPLES / 02
Make data ownership clear
Give each responsibility an owner. The interface
presents state. An application service coordinates a
workflow. Persistence commits durable changes.
View Use case Storage
Passing a database object through every screen makes
boundaries difficult to change. Passing an immutable
document summary keeps rendering separate from
storage details.
Identify which layer should know about file paths, and
which should only know about a document identifier.
SHELF / ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 2

pages.canonicalText:
SHELF SAMPLES / 03
Caching is a tradeoff
A cache avoids repeating work, but introduces a
second representation that can become stale. Decide
what is authoritative, how entries are invalidated and
how much memory the cache may use.
PDF thumbnails are derived data. If a thumbnail
disappears, recreate it. Original documents and
private annotations are not disposable caches.
Original Thumbnail Display
Ask: can this information be recreated without asking
the user to do the work again?
SHELF / ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 3

pages.canonicalText:
SHELF SAMPLES / 04
Design the failure path
An import is not complete when a preview appears. It
is complete when the required data has been safely
stored and the operation has been acknowledged.
A recoverable design considers full storage,
interrupted writes, duplicate requests and corrupted
input. Error messages must tell the user what
happened without claiming that missing work was
saved.
This is original sample material illustrating general engineering reasoning.
The architecture and recovery semantics of this app are documented in the
source package.
Review exercise: sketch a save operation that can fail at
any step without overwriting the original.
SHELF / ORIGINAL SAMPLE NOTES 4
